executive_summary: The PCAP reveals a compromised internal Windows host (10.0.2.16) that performed rapid DNS lookups to legitimate domains (www.msftncsi.com, www.google.com, www.google.cz) and immediately opened HTTP connections to the resolved IPs, a classic blending technique used by the CTU‑13 botnet to hide C2 traffic in normal web traffic. The host also beacons on a ~14‑hour cadence to an external IP (66.36.228.41) and generated anomalous ICMP traffic (large packets, destination‑unreachable and TTL‑exceeded messages). The adversary’s objective is to maintain a stealthy command‑and‑control channel and potentially receive additional payloads or instructions.

attack_timeline.description: DNS query for www.msftncsi.com resolves to 193.45.10.144.
TCP connection from 10.0.2.16 to 193.45.10.144:80 within 0.077 s.
Second DNS query for www.msftncsi.com resolves again to 193.45.10.144; TCP connection follows within 0.001 s.
